hooks.text: A solar observatory became history's greatest comet hunter.
How did a Sun-staring satellite find over 5,000 comets?
Built to watch the Sun, it survived months frozen before finding 5,000 comets.

title: The Accidental Comet Hunter
description: Designed to monitor the Sun, the SOHO spacecraft accidentally discovered over 5,000 comets.

beats.text: A solar observatory became history's greatest comet hunter.
beats.visual: Artist concept of the SOHO spacecraft observing the Sun, ESA and NASA, 1995

beats.text: It was launched in 1995 for just a two-year mission.
beats.visual: Lockheed Martin Atlas IIAS rocket launching SOHO, 1995

beats.text: Then a command error sent it spinning into a silent, frozen deep-space blackout.
beats.visual: Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange point orbit diagram, NASA
queries: Sun Earth L1 Lagrange point diagram

beats.text: Engineers pulled off a miracle recovery using reaction wheels as virtual gyroscopes.
beats.visual: SOHO spacecraft hardware diagram showing reaction wheels

beats.text: Its LASCO instrument blocks the solar glare with an artificial eclipse.
beats.visual: SOHO LASCO C3 coronagraph image showing solar corona and comet, 2024

beats.text: That sun-blocking trick unlocked a staggering scale of discoveries.
beats.visual: Comet Tsuchinshan ATLAS captured in SOHO LASCO data, 2024

beats.text: Citizen scientists combing through public data found over 5,000 comets.
beats.visual: Citizen science online data analysis graphic, NASA

beats.text: More than half of all known comets were found by a solar observatory.
beats.visual: SOHO spacecraft in space artist impression, ESA NASA
queries: SOHO spacecraft artist impression ESA NASA
